learning_objective: The learner will attribute each of 8 vendor decisions to the pricing model, one-time or subscription, whose incentives make it more likely, scoring at least 7 of 8.
specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** licenses-vendor-incentive-explorer
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Analyze
**Bloom Verb:** attribute
**Learning Objective:** The learner will attribute each of 8 vendor decisions to the pricing model, one-time or subscription, whose incentives make it more likely, scoring at least 7 of 8. **Prerequisites:** one-time license, subscription license, recurring revenue, upgrade revenue, customer lifetime value, vendor incentives (defined in the chapter section "How Pricing Shapes Vendor Behavior"). **Evidence of Mastery:** The learner chooses One-time license or Subscription license for each of 8 decisions. A choice is correct when it equals the Correct model column in Content. Mastery is 7 of 8 correct on the first pass. Reading the revenue summaries is exploration and is not scored. **Misconceptions:** (1) Vendors behave the same way under every pricing model. (2) Subscription pricing only changes how customers pay and not what vendors build. **Instructional Rationale:** Attributing a decision to an incentive makes the learner trace a cause, which is the Analyze-level act, instead of memorizing which model is better. **Content:** The revenue summaries shown before the decisions: | Model | Where the next dollar comes from | The vendor's strongest incentive | |---|---|---| | One-time license | A new buyer or an upgrade purchase | Win new buyers and make upgrades look worth buying | | Subscription license | A renewal or a higher fee | Prevent cancellation and raise what each customer pays | The 8 decisions, in this fixed order: | # | Vendor decision shown | Correct model | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | Add a showy feature so owners feel they must buy the next version. | One-time license | Upgrade revenue depends on making the next version look new. | | 2 | Keep customers satisfied so they renew every year. | Subscription license | Each renewal is the next dollar, so keeping the customer matters. | | 3 | Charge for each major version. | One-time license | The sale of a version is the revenue event. | | 4 | Make cancellation steps long and hard to find. | Subscription license | Each canceled customer ends the recurring revenue. | | 5 | Stop fixing bugs in old versions to push owners to the new one. | One-time license | Owners of old versions pay nothing more until they upgrade. | | 6 | Raise the annual fee, expecting most customers to renew. | Subscription license | Customers who are locked in may pay more rather than switch. | | 7 | Compete mainly on the number of new customers won each quarter. | One-time license | Without renewals, revenue depends on new sales. | | 8 | Add reminders and features that bring users back every week. | Subscription license | Frequent use makes renewal feel worthwhile. | **Provenance:** All eight decisions are illustrative scenarios invented for this chapter and derived from the incentives defined in the chapter text; the sim labels them illustrative. **Rules:** Each decision is answered once. The score is the number of correct answers out of 8. Mastery is a score >= 7. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner reads the revenue summaries for the two models. 2. The learner reads decision 1 and chooses a model. 3. The sim shows right or wrong with the Why text. 4. The learner moves through decisions 2 to 8 and then sees the score. **Feedback:** Eight decisions in fixed order, one attempt each. Correct: "Correct" with the Why text. Incorrect: the correct model and the Why text. The final screen shows "n of 8" and the message "Mastery reached" when n >= 7. **Starting State:** Both revenue summaries are visible and decision 1 is shown. The question on screen is "Which pricing model makes this decision more likely?" **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter states that 10,000 customers at $30 per year produce about $300,000, that a five-year customer paying $30 per year is worth $150, and that the explorer has 8 decisions.
